title: Connecting CSS to HTML
summary: Style the same semantic profile page three ways—inline, internal, and external—then choose the cleanest method as the design grows.

sketchBlocks.title: Start with inline CSS: fast, local, and limited
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown: CSS can reach HTML in three common ways: **inline styles**, an internal **`

sketchBlocks.title: Move page-level rules into a <style> block
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
When several elements on **one page** need coordinated styling, repeating `style="..."` attributes becomes noisy. An internal stylesheet moves CSS into a **`<style>` element**, normally inside the document `<head>`:

```html
<style>
  h1 {
    color: #0f766e;
  }
</style>
```

This solves an organization problem: the page's styling rules live together instead of being scattered across individual tags. It is cleaner than inline CSS for one document, but a second HTML page cannot automatically reuse those rules.

**Line by line:** First, `<style>` opens the page's internal stylesheet. Second, `h1` selects the heading. Third, the braces hold its declaration block. Fourth, `color: #0f766e;` defines the text color. Finally, `</style>` ends the internal stylesheet.

The second task refactors the same page from inline styling to an internal stylesheet without changing the visual result.

sketchBlocks.title: Scale the same rule into an external stylesheet
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
As a site grows, keeping CSS inside every HTML document creates duplication. An **external stylesheet** moves reusable presentation rules into a separate file such as `styles.css`, then HTML links to it:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">
```

```css
h1 {
  color: #0f766e;
}
```

This separation solves the maintainability problem: multiple pages can share one visual system, and one change in `styles.css` can update every page that links to it. HTML stays focused on structure and meaning while the stylesheet carries reusable presentation.

**Line by line:** First, `<link` creates a relationship from the HTML document. Second, `rel="stylesheet"` tells the browser the linked resource contains CSS. Third, `href="styles.css"` names the stylesheet file. In `styles.css`, `h1` selects headings and the `color` declaration defines their presentation.

The third task uses both files: add the stylesheet link in `index.html`, then place the reusable rule in `styles.css`. From the next lesson onward, `styles.css` becomes the main editing surface unless a task explicitly needs an HTML class, id, stylesheet link, or inline-style change.

help.hint_2: External CSS does not require duplicated style blocks or rewritten page content.

quizDraft.title: Step 1: Make one inline style on the real portfolio
quizDraft.prompt:
## CSS setup task

The inherited Home page works, but the name heading still looks like untouched browser-default HTML. An inline declaration is useful here because it demonstrates a deliberately local one-element style before you build reusable CSS. Use the existing multi-page Jordan Lee portfolio exactly as it came from HTML Foundations. In `index.html`, give the Home-page `h1` an inline `color: #0f766e;`. Do not change the other pages, image, navigation, text, or structure. Check Home in the preview: only the Jordan Lee heading should turn teal, while every other page and element stays unchanged.

### File to edit

`index.html`

### Check your work

Keep the site's existing cumulative work, make the requested change, then compare the **Preview** with the **Expected result** before moving on.
quizDraft.hint: Make the change on the existing Home h1 itself; this first step is intentionally local.

quizDraft.title: Step 2: Refactor the same Home style into <style>
quizDraft.prompt:
## CSS setup task

The heading now has the right `color`, but presentation is mixed directly into the h1 markup. An internal style block keeps page-level presentation together while preserving the same visual result. Keep the same complete portfolio and the same visual result. Remove the inline style from the Home-page h1 and place an internal `<style>` block in `index.html` with `h1 { color: #0f766e; }`. Do not change the other files. Check the preview after refactoring: the Home heading should look exactly the same, but the h1 tag should return to clean semantic HTML.

### File to edit

`index.html`

### Check your work

Keep the site's existing cumulative work, make the requested change, then compare the **Preview** with the **Expected result** before moving on.
quizDraft.hint: Move the same declaration into the document head rather than changing the `color` value.

quizDraft.title: Step 3: Make the stylesheet reusable across the whole portfolio
quizDraft.prompt:
## CSS setup task

The Home page is styled, but the portfolio has four pages and a page-local style cannot become a shared visual system. An external stylesheet lets the entire site reuse one source of presentation while relative paths keep the nested Projects page connected correctly. Move the Home-page h1 rule out of the internal `<style>` block and into `styles.css`. Then connect the same stylesheet to the entire inherited portfolio: use `href="styles.css"` in `index.html`, `about.html`, and `contact.html`, and `href="../styles.css"` in `projects/portfolio.html`. Keep `images/profile.png` and all HTML content unchanged. This is the stylesheet the rest of CSS Foundations will grow. Open several pages in the preview: the shared stylesheet should load everywhere, and the Home h1 should keep the same teal result.

### File to edit

`index.html`

### Check your work

Keep the site's existing cumulative work, make the requested change, then compare the **Preview** with the **Expected result** before moving on.
quizDraft.hint: Root pages and the nested Projects page need different relative href paths to the same stylesheet.

help.concept: An external stylesheet lets the entire site reuse one source of presentation while relative paths keep the nested Projects page connected correctly.
help.hint_1: Root pages and the nested Projects page need different relative href paths to the same stylesheet.
help.hint_2: Open several pages in the preview: the shared stylesheet should load everywhere, and the Home h1 should keep the same teal result.
